Gabriella Scozzafava Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save Featured Newly FDA-approved UV filter offers additional sun protection options Gabriella Scozzafava Nov 13, 2026 Nov 13, 2026 Updated 52 mins ago 0 Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save Freshman finance major Charlie Scott and dermatologist at UCF Health Faculty Physician Practice Dr. Naveed Sami explain the health impacts of the newly FDA-approved sunscreen filter, bemotrizinol, which is reaching store shelves this year. This package aired in the Nov. 9 webcast. Anchored by Kathleen Moore. Gabriella Scozzafava Skincare brands are bringing new sunscreen products to shelves after the FDA approved bemotrizinol on June 9, 2026. The approval makes bemotrizinol the first new UV filter to be approved in the U.S. in more than two decades. UCF students often receive sun exposure from walking around campus, attending sports games and tailgates or going to university events, which can cause both short- and long-term damage to skin health. Now, students will have more sunscreen options to choose from as Neutrogena, Ultra Violette and La Roche-Posay launch some of the first products with bemotrizinol in the U.S. Dr. Naveed Sami, a dermatologist at UCF Health Faculty Physician Practice, said the new sunscreen is exciting because bemotrizinol offers benefits from the two main types of sunscreens: mineral or physical and chemical. “Bemotrizinol is unique in the sense it’s actually a chemical filter, but also with the properties of a physical sunscreen, so you may have the best of both worlds," Sami said. Mineral sunscreens are larger molecules that don’t get absorbed and work by deflecting UV light. The physical sunscreens are very photostable, meaning they don’t break down with sun exposure, but are more likely to leave a white cast appearance on the skin, Sami said. Freshman finance major Charlie Scott reviews a sunscreen bottle label during the men's club soccer team practice at the Recreation and Wellness Center Park on Nov. 3. After getting a sunburn from high UV exposure at the beach, Scott said he tries to apply sunscreen every day. Gabriella Scozzafava CeraVe's Invisible Mineral Face Sunscreen and Blue Lizard's Sheer Face Mineral Sunscreen Lotion are mineral sunscreen products. They both include mineral sunscreen active ingredients zinc oxide and titanium dioxide. Chemical sunscreens are smaller molecules, Sami said, and get absorbed into the skin, which then absorbs the sunlight. To remain as stable as a physical sunscreen, chemical sunscreens have to be mixed and matched, he said. Sami said that bemotrizinol is a larger molecule that will sit on the surface of the skin and works similarly to chemical sunscreens by absorbing and releasing the heat, but it doesn't get absorbed into the skin. Bemotrizinol is very photostable compared to other chemical sunscreens, does not leave a white cast, and provides a broad spectrum of UVA and UVB protection. While UV rays from the sun can stimulate vitamin D production in the skin, they also pose several risks, including sunburn, skin aging and skin cancer, according to the CDC . UCF students experience high levels of UV radiation throughout the school year. The monthly average UV index can reach 10 in Central Florida during months in both the fall and spring semesters, according to the Environmental Protection Agency . Freshman finance major Charlie Scott spends at least eight hours a week in the sun from playing for the men’s club soccer team. He said he takes preventing these UV exposure risks seriously. “Yeah, I do use sunblock a lot,” Scott said. “I use it, because I am a little bit scared of skin cancer. I do have family members that do have it.” Freshman finance major Charlie Scott practices with men's club soccer teammates at the Recreation and Wellness Center Park on Nov. 3. He said he almost always applies sunscreen before practices and games. Gabriella Scozzafava While bemotrizinol is new in the U.S., it is not new globally. Several countries, including Canada, Australia and countries in Europe and Asia, had already been using bemotrizinol for years. The approval process took longer in the U.S. because sunscreen is considered an over-the-counter drug here, unlike in many other countries, which consider it an over-the-counter cosmetic, Stanford Medicine reported . As a sunscreen user, Scott said he has faced wearability issues with sunscreens feeling thick and leaving a white cast on his skin. He said he is excited to have another option to choose from and is curious to see how his skin reacts to it. “I always feel like if there was almost a lighter product for me to use where it’s not so heavy on my skin, I would definitely be interested in that because I do know when I use sunblock, one of my fears is that it’s going to clog my face and cause like an acne breakout,” Scott said. While bemotrizinol products offer different advantages, Sami said the filter still has limitations. "It provides a significant amount of protection for the same amount of time that any sunscreen would," Sami said. "But like any chemical sunscreen, it has to be applied 15 to 20 minutes before going outside, as opposed to physical sunscreens, which actually work a lot more quicker, chemical sunscreens take a little bit longer to work."  Regardless of whether consumers choose to switch to bemotrizinol-based sunscreen products, Sami encourages students to follow regular sun safety habits, including wearing sunscreen lotions instead of sprays to ensure enough coverage, reapplying sunscreen often and wearing sun-protective clothing. "Get a sunscreen you like, and that you are going to use," Sami said. "That is absolutely crucial."
